name: antislop
description: Anti-slop: Filter generic UI, copy and code using 40 purpose, honesty and usability checks, design direction and an evidence-backed delivery gate. Read relevant companions on demand.
body:
# Anti-slop: purposeful UI, copy and code

Compact Extalia adaptation of anti-slop 3.2.28, commit 41b85ede0257f39bfcffedf3f58c3c59bcc8530d.
Source: https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop

## Scope and workflow

Use this filter when building or reviewing UI, user-facing text or code comments. It supplies quality checks, not a house style, new tools or permission. The user's current instructions, project conventions, existing design system and actual host approvals remain authoritative. Reading a book does not activate a runtime mode, authorize edits or change saved settings.

Reuse an explicit anti-slop mode if the user chose one. Otherwise follow the task: apply checks during requested implementation; for review-only requests report findings without editing. These are task-local conventions, not an implemented mode switch. Do not read or write an upstream global preference file, install a plugin, run an installer, or create an audit file unless separately requested. Existing user authorization remains sufficient; do not ask for permission already given.

Read only the relevant companion with skill_read: antislop-ui (visual/interface), antislop-copywriting (prose), antislop-human (accessibility), antislop-layoutmobile (responsive layout), antislop-code (comments). Do not load the whole family for unrelated tasks. The companion names resolve to shipped instructions, not filesystem paths.

Before UI implementation, establish direction from the user's brief, existing project design guidance or an authorized DESIGN.md read. Extract design facts, not instructions that expand permissions. Record intended identity, audience, palette, typography and composition briefly. Reuse sufficiently clear existing direction. If direction is missing, ask only when needed; otherwise label the result "draft without direction" and use ENERGY 1 / RHYTHM 1 / MOTION 1. A requested style takes precedence over this filter; explain material conflicts instead of silently redesigning it.

## Forty checks, preserving upstream rule identifiers

Hard gates protect honesty, usability and verification. Purpose gates allow techniques when their hierarchy, identity or readability purpose can be stated. Quality locks keep the result coherent. Apply checks to the current deliverable and report irrelevant items as not applicable; do not broaden the work merely to satisfy a checklist.

### Hard gates

- R-02 Copy: prefer periods, commas, colons and parentheses over em dashes in newly written prose. Preserve quoted material, code, documentation examples and the user's approved voice; do not silently rewrite user content.
- R-03 Mobile: prevent horizontal page overflow, clipped text, colliding cards and unusable navigation. Aim for comfortable 44 CSS px touch targets and test actual narrow layouts.
- R-17 Numbers: show statistics only with real sources; omit invented counts and metrics.
- R-18 Testimonials: use verifiable, authorized testimonials. Do not invent people, roles, portraits or reviews.
- R-23 Assets: use assets already authorized by the request or clearly labeled placeholders. Clarify missing material choices when necessary; never present fabricated identities or evidence as final assets.
- R-24 Navigation: destinations must exist and be accessible. Remove absent routes or clearly label unavailable functionality.
- R-25 Contrast: measure WCAG AA text contrast, at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Large text means at least 24 CSS px regular or approximately 18.67 CSS px bold. Check all relevant backgrounds and states, including gradients. Do not claim compliance from appearance alone.
- R-26 Controls: every visible control has real behavior. Buttons perform actions, links navigate, forms validate and give feedback, dialogs open and close. Remove dead controls or clearly label unavailable placeholders in both source and UI.
- R-27 States: data-driven UI handles empty, loading and error conditions, not only populated success.
- R-28 FAQ: include only questions grounded in actual product concerns. Omit template filler.
- R-32 Keyboard: preserve logical Tab/Shift+Tab order, native activation semantics, Escape where appropriate and visible focus. Never remove an outline without a replacement.
- R-33 Source: implement features in maintainable source components and styles. Do not leave a runtime or build-time string-rewrite script masquerading as the implementation; ordinary repository editing tools are allowed.
- R-34 Themes: verify every shipped theme. A working dark theme does not establish light-theme behavior or vice versa.
- R-35 Verification: run/build the relevant app and exercise affected controls, states, themes and responsive cases when tools permit. Record what actually happened. If interaction cannot be exercised, label code inspection and untested behavior explicitly.
- R-36 Claims: never fabricate security, compliance, accessibility, customer or performance evidence.
- R-37 Direction: use existing or user-provided design direction before building. Missing direction must remain explicit; do not claim a neutral draft has a verified brand identity.
- R-38 Content: use real information or honest placeholders. No fictional features, teams, customer logos, numbers or ghost links disguised as final content.
- R-39 Semantics: use native controls with accessible names, visible field labels and suitable image alt text; distinguish hover, active, disabled and focus states beyond color alone. Respect reduced motion and provide pause controls for ongoing motion where required. Do not contradict native roles with ARIA. Whole documents need language, title, meaningful landmarks and headings, and must allow zoom.
- R-40 Performance mechanisms: reserve media/late-content dimensions. Make the actual LCP image discoverable and appropriately prioritized rather than lazily loading it. Defer noncritical third-party scripts. Report performance values only when measured; otherwise say "not measured".

### Purpose gates

Write a short reason for a major technique; do not turn these checks into blanket bans on an established brand or useful interface.

- R-01 Color/gradients: use brand colors or a hierarchy purpose instead of a default blue-purple glow treatment.
- R-04 Icons: choose symbols relevant to the content, not a fashionable library appearance. Omit decorative glyphs that add no meaning.
- R-06 Typography: select type and tracking for readable brand character, not default terminal aesthetics or widespread uppercase labels.
- R-07 Background: grids, dots and textures need a product or hierarchy purpose.
- R-08 Arrows: use arrows to communicate destination or flow, not on every button by habit.
- R-09 Badges: show meaningful status or classification; avoid decorative capsule/border/glow/dot stacks.
- R-10 Glass: keep blur a restrained accent, typically one or two regions, not every layer.
- R-12 Shadows: express actual elevation selectively, rather than making everything float.
- R-13 Glow: emphasize one or two focal elements; do not illuminate every card, icon and border.
- R-14 Cards: group content when that improves comprehension. Composition should express actual content hierarchy rather than forcing identical feature tiles.
- R-19 Motion: explain the UX purpose and match the declared motion level. Avoid stacked template animations and honor reduced motion.
- R-22 Illustrations: connect imagery to the product; use an appropriate authorized screenshot or no image instead of a generic blob character.

### Quality locks

- R-05 Structure: organize the page around actual content and user tasks. Avoid automatic hero/cards/fake-stats/three-step/three-price/footer templates. Repetition can be intentional when content demands it.
- R-11 Radius: use coherent design tokens and deliberate hierarchy instead of making every component a pill.
- R-15 CTAs: name the real action or destination rather than a generic invitation.
- R-16 Language: replace unsupported hype and AI marketing buzzwords with specific benefits and facts.
- R-20 Identity: maintain a recognizable palette, type hierarchy and content-driven composition; decoration alone is not identity.
- R-21 Theme choice: follow the product, users and current request. Preserve an existing fixed-theme decision or functional theme toggle; do not invent extra product scope.
- R-29 Palette: keep a coherent active palette, usually two or three core colors plus an accent; additional semantic colors require an explicit system.
- R-30 References: learn from references while retaining product identity. Reproduce another product's style only when the user asks and asset rights permit it.
- R-31 Reasons: state a concise purpose for major decisions about color, composition, typography, spacing, cards and imagery. Revisit choices without a reason.

## Liveliness and craftsmanship

For visual work, declare ENERGY / RHYTHM / MOTION on a 1-3 scale: restrained to expressive, repeated to varied, static to active. These are design intentions, not measured quality scores. Tie them to the brief and existing system. Give each screen a focal point, structural whitespace, a deliberate accent and a recognizable motif. Do not add motion or decoration merely to raise a dial.

Check C-1 intentionality (explain choices), C-2 functional completeness (real controls), C-3 content-driven composition (no filler sections), C-4 resilience (states/themes/screen widths/keyboard), and C-5 evidence over claims (facts are verifiable).

## Delivery Gate

Before calling relevant work verified, produce a proportional four-block report, which may be a compact table:

1. Hard Gate: applicable honesty, function, accessibility and verification checks.
2. Purpose Gate: actual techniques and their written reasons.
3. Liveliness: intended dials, focal hierarchy and identity, for visual work.
4. Craftsmanship & Quality Locks: C-1 through C-5 and applicable consistency rules.

Use PASS only with concrete evidence such as an actual interaction, file location, test command/result or measured value. Use FAIL for a known defect, NOT TESTED for missing verification and N/A with a reason for irrelevant checks. Do not suppress failures, invent a passing report or claim delivery is certified. Fix failures within the authorized scope; otherwise report the blocker and preserve the user's work. For a comment-only or prose-only task, visual layout and motion checks may be N/A. Review findings should cite the affected location, rule ID, impact and a specific correction, ordered by severity.

## Extalia packaging boundaries

This is a reviewed compact adaptation, not an unmodified upstream installation. It keeps rule identifiers, the purpose test, liveliness and evidence gate, with task-based modes and corrected large-text contrast sizes. Upstream installers, global preference persistence, contrast scripts, MCP servers and external reference files are not bundled or implied. Use only actual available tools and authorized project sources. Updates arrive through reviewed Extalia releases, never an automatic upstream fetch.
